Hi Elliot —

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday. Per our MAP, next week we want to move from discovery to a short connectivity sprint so your team can exercise the evaluation flow end-to-end. High level ask: can we target API-key + org bootstrap, IP allowlist, and VPC peering readiness within a 10 business-day window once access is approved?

Proposed kickoff scope (we'll adjust based on your procurement timeline):
- Org bootstrap: create a MediCore org in the Private control plane, add two admin seats (security + platform).
- API keys: we’ll issue a scoped POC API key with 30-day expiry (ephemeral tokens recommended).
- IP allowlist: provide CIDR ranges for our worker pools; we’ll provide sample firewall rules.
- VPC peering: optional for production; for POC we can do VPN or secure transit.

I’ve attached a short connectivity diagram and a MAP checklist to map responsibilities. Marissa will follow up with exact CIDRs and a minimal peering recipe tomorrow.

Next steps:
1) Elliot — reply with a preferred start date and any procurement gating items (PO, MSA exceptions).
2) MediCore security — confirm whether you prefer peering (VPC) or IP allowlisting only for the POC.
3) Marissa — technical playbook and attachment.

Thanks,

Thanks, this looks sensible. A few clarifying Qs before we lock dates: 
- Can you confirm the exact outbound CIDR ranges we need to allow? Our networking team needs /24s if possible to keep rules tight.
- For the ephemeral API key — will the key be tied to an org admin or scoped to the POC namespace? We prefer least privilege.

Thanks Elliot — quick answers and a minimal recipe below. Quoting your questions inline.

> - Can you confirm the exact outbound CIDR ranges we need to allow? Our networking team needs /24s if possible to keep rules tight.

We run inference from managed worker pools across two regions for redundancy. For the POC we can allocate a small, static set of egress ranges — the recommended minimal allowlist is:
- 34.210.128.0/24 (primary-west)
- 34.211.0.0/24 (primary-east)

If you need single /24 per region we can provide those exact ranges; we’ll also supply a short-lived alternate range for testing.

> - For the ephemeral API key — will the key be tied to an org admin or scoped to the POC namespace? We prefer least privilege.

We will issue a scoped POC API key that is bound to the MediCore POC org namespace and limited to generation + embeddings for the trial models only. Lifecycle: 30-day auto-expiry; renewable via portal or API (token exchange). We can provide a service-account style token for CI usage (rotatable).

> - VPC peering: we have strict peering approval timelines (security must review). For the POC, would an IP allowlist + mutual TLS endpoint be sufficient?

Yes — for the evaluation phase we commonly accept IP allowlist + enforced mTLS to our public ingestion endpoint. If you want private connectivity later we can open a peering ticket with network playbooks and an estimated 3–4 week lead time (dependent on cloud provider approvals).

Minimal peering checklist (for later phases):
1) Exchange account IDs and routing prefixes.
2) Test with a single subnet and strict security groups.
3) Validate KV cache behavior across peered route (we provide small stress script).

I attached an editable connectivity checklist and the network diagram referenced by Soojin. Let me know if you want a short walkthrough call (15–20 min) to walk your network/security team through the steps.

Cheers,
— Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
